name: Build a fee structure for a class or section and have it approved before it can be billed
priorityReason: Nothing can be invoiced until a structure exists and is approved. Every figure in the fee module comes from here.

goal.capability: to define what each student owes and have it approved before anything is billed against it
goal.outcome: invoices are raised from a figure somebody agreed to, not one somebody typed

secondaryActors.involvement: Approves the structure and every later change to it. Nothing is billable without that approval.
Is billed according to the approved structure, and never sees this screen.

additional.description: A new academic session opens and its fee structures are built before any invoice can be raised.
A class is created and has no structure yet, so it cannot be billed.

preconditions.condition: The class exists for the academic session, with its type set as Fixed or Subject Wise.
For a Subject Wise structure, the class carries the subjects the amounts will be set against.
An authenticated session exists and the acting user is Accounts or School Admin.
The fee types the structure will use exist, or are created while building it.

postConditions: An approved structure exists for the class or section and is the basis of every invoice raised against it.
The structure carries an effective date, so what a student owed in September can still be worked out in March.
A change to an approved structure exists as a new version with its own effective date, and the previous version is kept.
Invoices already issued are untouched. A structure change never rewrites a bill a family has already been given.
The approval is recorded with who gave it and when, so a figure on a family's invoice can be traced to somebody's decision.
A structure awaiting approval is not billable, and an invoice run against that class will find nothing to bill.
No invoice is raised by approving a structure. A structure is a price list, not a bill.

dataFields.name: Class
dataFields.validation: An active class in the current academic session.

dataFields.name: Scope
dataFields.validation: Whether the structure applies to every section of the class or to one section only (BR-2).

dataFields.name: Section
dataFields.validation: Required where the scope is one section.

dataFields.name: Structure type
dataFields.validation: Fixed prices the class as a whole; Subject Wise prices each subject. Both may be set against the same class (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Fee type
dataFields.validation: Tuition, admission, transport, examination and so on. Required for a Fixed structure.

dataFields.name: Amount
dataFields.validation: Greater than zero, in the smallest currency unit. One amount per fee type for Fixed, one per subject for Subject Wise (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Recurrence
dataFields.validation: How often the amount is billed. Decides what an invoice run produces for a billing period.

dataFields.name: Subject
dataFields.validation: Each subject the class carries is listed and priced. Required for a Subject Wise structure (BR-5).
dataFields.requiredWhen: The structure type is Subject Wise

dataFields.name: Effective from
dataFields.validation: The date the structure applies from. Not before the academic session start (BR-7).

dataFields.name: Version
dataFields.validation: Incremented each time an approved structure is changed. Earlier versions are kept (BR-8).

dataFields.name: Change reason
dataFields.validation: Maximum 500 characters. Required when changing an approved structure (BR-9).
dataFields.example: Tuition raised 8% for the 2026-27 session, approved by the board.
dataFields.requiredWhen: An approved structure is being changed

dataFields.name: Return reason
dataFields.validation: Maximum 500 characters. Required when returning a structure unapproved.
dataFields.example: Transport amount does not match the route pricing.

businessRules.rule: A structure is not billable until it is approved. An invoice run finds nothing to bill against a class whose structure is still in draft or awaiting approval.
A structure applies to every section of a class, or to one section only. A section-scoped structure overrides the class one for that section.
A class may carry both a Fixed structure and a Subject Wise one. A tuition fee charged to everybody and a per-subject laboratory charge are not alternatives.
Every amount is greater than zero and is held in the smallest currency unit. A free subject is expressed by not pricing it, not by pricing it at zero.
A Subject Wise structure lists every subject the class carries and prices each one. A subject added to the class afterwards is unpriced until the structure is versioned.
Accounts cannot approve their own structure. Building the price list and agreeing to it are separate acts by separate people.
Every structure carries an effective date, and it cannot be before the academic session starts. Without it, what a student owed in September cannot be worked out in March.
A change to an approved structure creates a new version with its own effective date. The previous version is kept, so an invoice raised under it remains explicable.
A change to an approved structure requires a written reason and goes through the same approval as the original.
A structure change never recalculates invoices already issued. A family given a bill is not re-billed because the price list moved afterwards.
Two approved structures for the same class and scope may not have overlapping effective periods. The new version's effective date closes the previous one.
Approving a structure raises no invoice. A structure is a price list; billing is a separate, deliberate act.

transitions.condition: Approved. It becomes billable from its effective date (BR-1).
A later version is approved and its effective date arrives (BR-8, BR-11).

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Fee → Fee structures → Build structure
basicFlow.userAction: Selects the class, and whether the structure covers every section or one section only.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Loads the class with its type and its subjects.

basicFlow.userAction: Sets the structure as Fixed or Subject Wise, or builds both against the same class.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Offers fee types for a Fixed structure, and the class's subjects for a Subject Wise one.

basicFlow.userAction: Enters the amount and recurrence against each fee type, or against each subject.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires every subject to be priced for a Subject Wise structure, and every amount to be above zero.

basicFlow.navigation: Build fee structure → Effective date → Submit for approval
basicFlow.userAction: Sets the effective date and submits the structure.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the effective date is not before the session start, then sets the structure to Awaiting approval.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Fee → Fee structures → Structure approval
basicFlow.userAction: Reviews the structure line by line and approves it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the approval with who gave it and when, and makes the structure billable from its effective date.
Makes the structure the basis for every invoice raised for that class or section from its effective date, and supersedes any earlier version.

basicFlow.navigation: Fee structures → Open → Create new version
basicFlow.userAction: Changes an approved structure later, giving a written reason and a new effective date.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Creates a new version at Draft, keeps the previous one, and leaves invoices already issued untouched.

alternateFlows.behaviour: Every subject the class carries is listed and each is priced. A student's bill is then the sum of the subjects they actually take (BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: The class carries both a flat charge and per-subject charges
alternateFlows.behaviour: A Fixed structure and a Subject Wise one are both built against the class. They are added together at invoicing, not treated as alternatives (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: One section is priced differently from the rest of its class
alternateFlows.behaviour: A section-scoped structure is built and overrides the class structure for that section only (BR-2).

alternateFlows.condition: The School Admin does not accept the structure
alternateFlows.navigation: Structure approval → Return with a reason
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns to Accounts with a written reason and is not billable. Nothing has been priced against the class in the meantime (BR-1).

alternateFlows.condition: Fees rise for the coming session
alternateFlows.navigation: Fee structures → Open → Create new version
alternateFlows.behaviour: A new version is built with its own effective date and goes through the same approval. Invoices already issued under the previous version are untouched (BR-8, BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: A subject is added to the class after the structure was approved
alternateFlows.navigation: Fee structures → Open → Create new version → Subjects
alternateFlows.behaviour: The new subject is unpriced until a new version is built and approved, so it is not silently billed at zero (BR-5).

openQuestions.question: Who maintains the fee type list — Accounts or School Admin?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. It decides who can invent a new charge.

openQuestions.question: May a structure be built for a future academic session before it opens?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and schools usually set next year's fees before the year starts.

openQuestions.question: Should the Principal approve a fee increase above a certain percentage, rather than the School Admin?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. A fee rise is a governance matter as much as an administrative one.

openQuestions.question: Is a section-scoped structure ever used in practice, or is pricing always per class?
openQuestions.assumption: The feature allows both. Confirm whether the school needs section pricing.

openQuestions.question: How is a subject a student does not take handled in a Subject Wise class — omitted, or billed at zero?
openQuestions.assumption: Omitted. It is not on their invoice at all.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
